"""v11 C4/L04: node-identity FIFO tabu on the plateau search (new file, no frozen edits).

Direction lock `docs/temporary/RLNN_v11_Direction_Locked.md` §3 wants the *action*
tabu of L04 (AlphaZero+Tabu, IJCAI 2024, PDF p.5 §5 + Alg.1) instead of the
node-level "forbidden" of v10.

Two corrections over the first v11 draft (both from the captain's code review of
2026-11-17 14:40, m01061):

* the draft keyed the FIFO on ``tuple(action.removed)`` and rejected a candidate
  only when an *identical removed set* had just been executed.  Exchange actions
  almost never repeat a removed set, so the FIFO could not fire: ER was 0 for
  every depth h and the six h rows were bit-identical.  L04's tabu list lives on
  **node identity** (a node just evicted may not be re-added within h steps, a
  node just added may not be evicted within h steps), not on action identity;
* the measured quantity must therefore be defined with the node-level
  intersection, and the probe has to report how often the intersection was
  non-empty (``hits``) next to the pool sizes.

``TabuList`` implements that list.  Two intersection conventions are provided so
the probe can report both:

``cross`` (default, L04 Alg.1)
    forbid when ``set(action.added) & recently_removed`` or
    ``set(action.removed) & recently_added`` is non-empty.  This is the classic
    move-tabu pair: the *undo* of the last h exchanges is forbidden, which is
    precisely the "do not walk straight back" rule the direction lock asks for.
``same``
    forbid when ``set(action.added) & recently_added`` or
    ``set(action.removed) & recently_removed`` is non-empty (the literal reading
    of the review comment).  Kept for completeness; on a walk that alternates
    add/remove of different nodes it fires much less often.

Metric definitions (also written into the probe JSON, direction lock §3.4):

``ER`` elimination rate
    ``ER = 1 - |pool_tabu| / |pool_plain|``, evaluated **paired** on the same
    ``(graph, state, outer round)``.  Denominator = number of macro rounds in
    which a candidate pool was actually built; each round contributes its own
    ratio (``er_rounds`` says how many).  ``er_pooled = 1 -
    sum(pool_tabu)/sum(pool_plain)`` is reported next to it so a single huge pool
    cannot dominate.
``AR`` acceptance rate
    ``AR = (rounds with size_after == size_before and mask changed and archive
    NOT refreshed) / outer_rounds``.  The "not refreshed" clause is what makes
    AR measure *walking* rather than *improving*: a round that improves the
    archive is not a plateau walk.  ``refreshed_rounds`` is reported separately
    because "no refresh in 8 rounds" is the second half of the C4 sentence.

**AR is a mechanism metric only** (t11 §3.6 closure): ``AR ~ 0.99`` says "the walk
happens" -- it is the same value with and without tabu -- and must never be read
as "exploration is sufficient" or as a gain.  The only gain metrics are ``gain``
and ``refreshed_rounds``.

Why a separate module: ``models/mis_v3_search.py`` is on the frozen list, and the
existing code has two structural gaps that this module fills without touching it

* ``models/mis_v3_search.py:197 candidate_actions`` forbids only the exact reverse
  of the actions in ``tabu`` (depth 1) -- "do not undo immediately", not "do not
  repeat recently";
* ``models/mis_v3_search.py:247 repair()`` has no ``tabu`` parameter at all, so
  every destroy-repair converges back to the same local optimum (the code-level
  cause of the v10 "same solution in 20/20 graphs" result).

Everything here is a thin wrapper/re-implementation over the frozen primitives
(``graph._exchanges``, ``graph.apply``, ``candidate_actions``, ``rollout``), so a
probe can measure the walk without changing the deployment path.
"""
from collections import deque
from math import inf
from time import perf_counter

from mis_v3_search import CandidatePool, RepairResult, SearchResult, candidate_actions, choose_action


class _Entry:
    """Minimal action record: the FIFO only needs the two node tuples."""

    __slots__ = ("added", "removed")

    def __init__(self, added=(), removed=()):
        self.added = tuple(added)
        self.removed = tuple(removed)

    def __repr__(self):
        return f"_Entry(added={self.added}, removed={self.removed})"


class TabuList:
    """Node-identity FIFO of depth ``h`` over executed exchange actions (L04 Alg.1)."""

    def __init__(self, h, mode="cross"):
        if mode not in ("cross", "same"):
            raise ValueError(f"unknown tabu mode {mode!r}")
        self.h = int(h)
        self.mode = mode
        self.fifo = deque(maxlen=self.h) if self.h else None
        self.added = set()
        self.removed = set()
        self.checks = 0
        self.hits = 0
        self.sample = None

    # -- state ---------------------------------------------------------------
    def __bool__(self):
        return bool(self.fifo)

    def __len__(self):
        return len(self.fifo) if self.fifo is not None else 0

    def clear(self):
        if self.fifo is not None:
            self.fifo.clear()
        self.added.clear()
        self.removed.clear()

    def push(self, action):
        """Record an executed action; the sets are rebuilt so eviction is exact."""
        if self.fifo is None:
            return
        self.fifo.append((tuple(action.added), tuple(action.removed)))
        self.added = {node for added, _ in self.fifo for node in added}
        self.removed = {node for _, removed in self.fifo for node in removed}

    # -- query ---------------------------------------------------------------
    def forbids(self, action):
        if self.fifo is None or not self.fifo:
            return False
        self.checks += 1
        added = set(action.added)
        removed = set(action.removed)
        if self.mode == "cross":
            hit = (added & self.removed) or (removed & self.added)
        else:
            hit = (added & self.added) or (removed & self.removed)
        if hit:
            self.hits += 1
            if self.sample is None:
                self.sample = dict(mode=self.mode,
                                   action_added=sorted(added), action_removed=sorted(removed),
                                   tabu_added=sorted(self.added), tabu_removed=sorted(self.removed),
                                   intersect=sorted(hit))
            return True
        return False

    def stats(self):
        return dict(h=self.h, mode=self.mode, depth=len(self), checks=self.checks,
                    hits=self.hits, sample=self.sample)


def improving_actions_tabu(graph, selected, *, cap=48, anchor=None, deadline=inf, tabu=None):
    """``improving_actions`` minus the actions the node-identity FIFO forbids.

    Mirrors the frozen rule (prefer size-1 exchanges; fall back to size-2 only when
    the size-1 list is empty) but filters *before* the cap, otherwise tabu would be
    applied to an already-truncated pool and the measured rejection rate would be
    meaningless.
    """
    for size in (1, 2):
        found = []
        for action in graph._exchanges(selected, size, deadline):
            if anchor is not None and anchor not in action.removed:
                continue
            if tabu is not None and tabu.forbids(action):
                continue
            found.append(action)
            if len(found) >= cap:
                break
        if found or size == 2:
            return found
    return []


def repair_tabu(graph, selected, *, tabu=None, rounds=4, cap=48, anchor=None,
                deadline=inf, extend_first=True):
    """``models/mis_v3_search.py:247 repair()`` with the node-identity FIFO.

    The executed action of every inner round is pushed onto ``tabu`` (shared across
    outer rounds by the caller), which is what the frozen ``repair()`` lacks.
    """
    result = RepairResult(selected)
    if perf_counter() >= deadline:
        result.deadline_hit = True
        return result
    if extend_first:
        candidate = graph.extend(selected)
        if perf_counter() >= deadline:
            result.deadline_hit = True
            return result
        result.work = candidate
    for _ in range(rounds):
        actions = improving_actions_tabu(graph, result.work, cap=cap, anchor=anchor,
                                         deadline=deadline, tabu=tabu)
        result.candidate_counts.append(len(actions))
        if perf_counter() >= deadline:
            result.deadline_hit = True
            return result
        if not actions:
            result.exhausted = True
            return result
        action = actions[0]
        candidate = graph.apply(result.work, action)
        if perf_counter() >= deadline:
            result.deadline_hit = True
            return result
        result.work = candidate
        result.exchanges += 1
        if tabu is not None:
            tabu.push(action)
    result.capped = True
    return result


def pool_plain_and_tabu(graph, selected, *, tabu=None, cap=32, anchored=False,
                        history=(), deadline=inf):
    """Candidate pool without and with the FIFO, paired on the same state.

    Returns ``(plain_pool, tabu_pool, rejected)`` where ``rejected`` counts the
    plain actions the FIFO removed (the numerator behind ``ER``).
    """
    plain = candidate_actions(graph, selected, cap=cap, anchored=anchored,
                             tabu=history, deadline=deadline)
    if tabu is None or not tabu:
        return plain, plain, 0
    kept = [action for action in plain.actions if not tabu.forbids(action)]
    return plain, CandidatePool(kept, len(kept), plain.completed), len(plain.actions) - len(kept)


def platform_search_tabu(graph, selected, *, tabu=None, fifo=None, choose="coverage",
                         outer_rounds=8, initial_rounds=3, horizon=2, candidate_cap=32,
                         improving_cap=48, repair_rounds=4, anchored=False, history=(),
                         deadline=inf, trailing=2, on_round=None):
    """``models/mis_v3_search.py:340 platform_search()`` with node-identity tabu.

    ``fifo`` is an alias of ``tabu`` (the reviewer's spelling).

    Passing ``tabu=None``/``fifo=None`` means "no memory": the call is delegated to
    the frozen ``mis_v3_search.platform_search`` unchanged, so the two are bit for
    bit identical (gates selftest item 10).  An *empty* ``TabuList`` instead takes
    the loop below, which additionally appends the executed action to ``history``
    (the probe's h=0 control keeps that bookkeeping).

    Differences from the frozen version once a FIFO is supplied, all additive:
    * the FIFO threads through ``repair_tabu``, the candidate pool and
      ``rollout_tabu``;
    * every outer round reports ``(size_before, size_after, changed, refreshed,
      pool_plain, pool_tabu, rejected)`` through ``on_round`` so the probe can
      compute ER and AR.  (No callback fires on the ``tabu=None`` delegation.)

    Deadline semantics are the frozen ones (``deadline=inf`` disables all clock
    reasoning); the probe runs with ``deadline=inf`` so that all 8 rounds happen
    and AR is measured on a fixed denominator.
    """
    if tabu is None:
        tabu = fifo
    elif fifo is not None:
        raise ValueError('pass either tabu= or fifo=, not both')
    if tabu is None:
        from mis_v3_search import platform_search as frozen_platform_search
        return frozen_platform_search(graph, selected, choose=choose,
                                      outer_rounds=outer_rounds,
                                      initial_rounds=initial_rounds, horizon=horizon,
                                      candidate_cap=candidate_cap,
                                      improving_cap=improving_cap,
                                      repair_rounds=repair_rounds, anchored=anchored,
                                      history=history, deadline=deadline)
    limited = deadline != inf
    work_deadline = deadline - 0.002 if limited else inf
    initial = (repair_tabu(graph, selected, tabu=tabu, rounds=initial_rounds,
                           cap=improving_cap, deadline=work_deadline, extend_first=False)
               if initial_rounds else RepairResult(selected))
    result = SearchResult(initial.work, initial.work, tuple(history)[-trailing:],
                          selected.bit_count(), initial.work.bit_count(),
                          exchanges=initial.exchanges, deadline_hit=initial.deadline_hit)
    for step in range(outer_rounds):
        if result.deadline_hit or (limited and perf_counter() >= work_deadline):
            result.deadline_hit = True
            break
        before = result.work
        began = perf_counter()
        strict = improving_actions_tabu(graph, result.work, cap=1, deadline=work_deadline,
                                        tabu=tabu)
        pool_plain = pool_tabu = rejected = None
        if strict:
            segment = repair_tabu(graph, before, tabu=tabu, rounds=repair_rounds,
                                  cap=improving_cap, deadline=work_deadline)
            result.work = segment.work
            result.exchanges += segment.exchanges
            result.deadline_hit = segment.deadline_hit
            kind = "repair"
        else:
            plain, pool, rejected = pool_plain_and_tabu(graph, before, tabu=tabu, cap=candidate_cap,
                                                        anchored=anchored, history=result.history,
                                                        deadline=work_deadline)
            pool_plain, pool_tabu = len(plain.actions), len(pool.actions)
            if not pool.completed:
                result.deadline_hit = True
                break
            if not pool.actions:
                break
            action = (choose(graph, before, pool.actions, (outer_rounds - step) / outer_rounds)
                      if callable(choose) else choose_action(graph, before, pool.actions, choose))
            result.history = (result.history + (action,))[-trailing:]
            macro = rollout_tabu(graph, before, action, tabu=tabu, horizon=horizon,
                                 repair_rounds=repair_rounds, improving_cap=improving_cap,
                                 candidate_cap=candidate_cap, deadline=work_deadline)
            result.work = macro.work
            result.exchanges += macro.exchanges
            result.neutral_decisions += len(macro.attempted_actions)
            result.deadline_hit = macro.deadline_hit
            kind = "macro"
        after = result.work
        refreshed = after.bit_count() > result.best.bit_count()
        if refreshed:
            result.best = after
        if on_round is not None:
            on_round(dict(round=step, kind=kind, size_before=before.bit_count(),
                          size_after=after.bit_count(), changed=after != before,
                          refreshed=refreshed, seconds=perf_counter() - began,
                          pool_plain=pool_plain, pool_tabu=pool_tabu, rejected=rejected))
        result.trace.append(dict(round=step, kind=kind, size=after.bit_count()))
        if result.deadline_hit:
            break
    result.outer_steps = len(result.trace)
    return result


def rollout_tabu(graph, selected, action, *, tabu=None, horizon=2, repair_rounds=4,
                 improving_cap=48, candidate_cap=32, deadline=inf):
    """``models/mis_v3_search.py:282 rollout()`` with the FIFO threaded through repair."""
    from mis_v3_search import RolloutResult

    result = RolloutResult(selected, selected, 0)
    attempted = [action]
    work = graph.apply_move(selected, action)
    anchor = action.added[0] if len(action.removed) == 2 else None
    for stage in range(horizon):
        if stage:
            strict = improving_actions_tabu(graph, work, cap=1, deadline=deadline, tabu=tabu)
            if not strict:
                _, pool, _ = pool_plain_and_tabu(graph, work, tabu=tabu, cap=candidate_cap,
                                                 history=(action,), deadline=deadline)
                if not pool.completed or not pool.actions:
                    break
                second = choose_action(graph, work, pool.actions)
                work = graph.apply_move(work, second)
                attempted.append(second)
        segment = repair_tabu(graph, work, tabu=tabu, rounds=repair_rounds,
                              cap=improving_cap, anchor=anchor if stage == 0 else None,
                              deadline=deadline)
        work = segment.work
        result.segments += 1
        result.exchanges += segment.exchanges
        result.capped |= segment.capped
        if work.bit_count() > result.best.bit_count():
            result.best = work
        if segment.deadline_hit:
            result.deadline_hit = True
            break
    result.ended_below_start = work.bit_count() < selected.bit_count()
    result.rolled_back = work.bit_count() < result.best.bit_count()
    result.work = result.best if result.rolled_back else work
    result.returned_to_start = result.work == selected
    result.attempted_actions = tuple(attempted)
    result.neutral_actions = () if result.rolled_back else tuple(attempted)
    result.gain = result.best.bit_count() - selected.bit_count()
    return result


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# self test (captain's diagnostic (1): a construction that *must* fire tabu)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
def self_test(verbose=True):
    """Assert the FIFO actually rejects candidates (``pool_tabu`` strict subset).

    Part A is synthetic and deterministic: the undo of an exchange must be
    forbidden in ``cross`` mode and allowed in ``same`` mode, which pins down the
    semantics the probe reports.

    Part B runs on a real RB graph: build the candidate pool of a real state, mark
    the "added" node of one pool action as recently evicted (that is exactly the
    situation after executing it), and require that the action disappears from the
    tabu pool while the plain pool still contains it.
    """
    undo = (_Entry(added=(7,), removed=(3,)), _Entry(added=(3,), removed=(7,)))
    executed, inverse = undo
    results = {}
    for mode in ("cross", "same"):
        tabu = TabuList(8, mode=mode)
        tabu.push(executed)
        results[mode] = tabu.forbids(inverse)
    if verbose:
        print(f"[A] undo forbidden: cross={results['cross']} same={results['same']}")
    if not results["cross"]:
        raise SystemExit("self_test: cross mode must forbid the undo of an exchange")

    import torch

    from mis_v3_search import SearchGraph

    # deterministic synthetic graph (no dataset / no torch_geometric needed): a
    # union of cycles, i.e. a 4-regular-ish sparse graph with a non-trivial MIS
    nodes = 120
    edges = []
    for offset in (1, 7, 31):
        for node in range(nodes):
            edges.append((node, (node + offset) % nodes))
    edge_index = torch.tensor(edges, dtype=torch.long).t().contiguous()
    graphs = [SearchGraph(nodes, edge_index, seed=1017)]
    checked = fired = 0
    for index, graph in enumerate(graphs):
        start = 0
        for node in sorted(range(graph.num_nodes), key=lambda n: graph.neighbors[n].bit_count()):
            if not graph.neighbors[node] & start:
                start |= 1 << node
        plain, _, _ = pool_plain_and_tabu(graph, start, tabu=None, cap=32)
        if not plain.actions:
            continue
        action = plain.actions[0]
        tabu = TabuList(8, mode="cross")
        tabu.push(_Entry(added=(), removed=action.added))     # "that node was just evicted"
        plain2, pool2, rejected = pool_plain_and_tabu(graph, start, tabu=tabu, cap=32)
        checked += 1
        strict = len(pool2.actions) < len(plain2.actions)
        fired += int(strict and rejected > 0)
        if verbose:
            print(f"[B] graph {index}: |pool|={len(plain2.actions)} "
                  f"|pool_tabu|={len(pool2.actions)} rejected={rejected} strict={strict}")
        if not strict:
            raise SystemExit(f"self_test: FIFO did not shrink the pool on graph {index}")
    if not checked:
        raise SystemExit("self_test: no candidate pool was built")
    return dict(cross_forbids_undo=results["cross"], same_forbids_undo=results["same"],
                graphs_checked=checked, graphs_strict_subset=fired)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    print(self_test())

FILE: models/mis_v11_unroll.py

"""v11 C3 -- size-aware unroll objective (decoder-in-the-loop, straight-through).

Paper question
--------------
The frozen one-step ``erdoes`` objective never sees the decoder, so the policy gets
no signal about *how many nodes its states can be completed to*.  v11 C3 rolls the
deploy-active sampler forward for ``unroll_steps`` update steps, decodes the state
every ``decode_every`` steps with the Appendix-A.3 gradient flip, and back-propagates
``-mean(decoded size)`` through the *last* decode only (straight-through: the flip
decision is discrete, the sigmoid probability carries the gradient).

Everything here is new code.  ``models/mis_v11_unroll.py`` is imported by an additive
``elif self.loss == 'unroll'`` branch in ``models/solvers.py``; the file:line ledger
lives in ``docs/temporary/RLNN_v11_Implementation.md``.  ``models/models.py``,
``models/mis_v8_pad.py`` (deployment) and the other frozen modules are untouched.

Contract
--------
* t4 MATLAB input I5: the mean waiting time to a +1 improvement is 517 steps, a
  40-step window covers 0 %/7.7 % of the gains and 200 steps 43.2 %
  => default ``unroll_steps = 200``.
* captain 2026-11-17: keep 200 unless the adaptive gates trip
  (peak GPU memory > 6 GB or per-graph fwd+bwd > 0.6 s) -> fall back to 128 and
  record ``degraded_reason`` in ``run.json``.
* decode cadence stays every 10 steps, only the last decode keeps autograd.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import json
from datetime import datetime, timezone
from pathlib import Path
from time import perf_counter

import torch

DEFAULT_STEPS = 200
FALLBACK_STEPS = 128
DECODE_EVERY = 10
MEMORY_GATE_BYTES = 6 * 1024 ** 3
TIME_GATE_SECONDS = 0.6


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
# rollout
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
def _rand(shape, *, dtype, device, generator):
    if generator is None:
        return torch.rand(shape, dtype=dtype, device=device)
    return torch.rand(shape, dtype=dtype, device=device, generator=generator)


def _dense(tensor, like=None):
    """Densify a CSR adjacency (or a tensor topology) and match ``like.dtype``.

    ``models/mis_v1.py::adjacency`` and ``solvers.policy_topology`` hand back a
    sparse CSR matrix.  The A.3 decode multiplies by it with ``fp16`` operands,
    and cuSparse rejects that mix on the deployed cards
    (``cusparseSpMM_bufferSize(): data type combination not supported,
    matA: CUDA_R_16F, matB: CUDA_R_32F``).  The deployment arm already runs the
    dense kernel (``models/mis_v8_pad.py:80 self.dense_norm``), so densifying
    here is the same operator, just without the CSR path; the dtype cast is what
    ``dense_norm`` is built with (``self.dtype``).
    """
    if not isinstance(tensor, torch.Tensor):
        return tensor
    if tensor.layout != torch.strided:
        tensor = tensor.to_dense()
    if like is not None and tensor.dtype != like.dtype:
        tensor = tensor.to(like.dtype)
    return tensor


def decode_size(problem, state, adjacency, bias):
    """A.3 gradient-flip decode of every column; returns ``(sizes, decoded)``."""
    decoded = problem.decode_gradient_flip(state, _dense(adjacency, state),
                                           _dense(bias, state), return_solutions=True)
    return decoded.sum(dim=0), decoded


def unroll(solver, graph, adjacency, topology, x0, *, steps, decode_every=DECODE_EVERY,
           generator=None, logits_bias=None, archive=False, keep_grad=True):
    """Roll the deploy-active sampler ``steps`` update steps from ``x0``.

    The dynamics are the deployment dynamics of ``models/mis_v8_pad.py::_body``
    (flip with probability ``sigmoid(logits)``, noise shape ``(num_nodes, K)``),
    without the tabu mask that only the LNS path enables.
    """
    problem = solver.problem
    bias = graph.b
    adjacency = _dense(adjacency, x0)
    topology = _dense(topology, x0)
    x = x0
    sizes, logits_last = [], None
    best_mask = best_size = None
    decode_steps = []
    last_size = None
    for step in range(steps):
        product = (adjacency @ x.detach()) if getattr(solver, 'structure_gain', False) else None
        # The policy input is detached as well, so the gradient of one step sees a
        # fixed state: with the carrier left on the input, the model Jacobian is
        # re-applied once per step and the parameter gradient still grows ~3x/step
        # (measured 1.1e4 at 10 steps -> 7.1e12 at 40 -> NaN at 128 in fp32).
        logits = solver.flip_logits(x.detach(), graph, adjacency, topology,
                                    adjacency_product=product)
        if logits_bias is not None:
            logits = logits + logits_bias
        prob = torch.sigmoid(logits)
        rr = _rand(x.shape, dtype=x.dtype, device=x.device, generator=generator)
        # Forward value: the deployment flip rule, bit for bit.  ``x.detach()`` in
        # both branches matters: the ``where`` branches have unit Jacobian in ``x``,
        # so leaving them on the graph makes the parameter gradient compound once per
        # step (measured: 4.1e4 at 10 steps -> 1.9e14 at 40 -> NaN at 128 in fp32).
        flip = torch.where(rr < prob, 1 - x.detach(), x.detach())
        # Straight-through carrier: the frozen ``erdoes`` relaxation
        # ``(1-p)x + p(1-x)`` has expectation ``flip`` and derivative (1-2x) dp,
        # so adding the *detached* difference changes no forward bit but lets the
        # gradient reach ``prob`` -- ``torch.where`` alone would cut it (the
        # comparison is boolean, not differentiable).
        # ``x.detach()`` keeps the surrogate *one-step*: crediting only the current
        # logits.  Letting the state path carry gradient makes the parameter Jacobian
        # compound once per step and the gradient explode geometrically (measured on
        # GPU1, fp32, K=20: max |param grad| 1.1e5 at 10 steps, 3.2e20 at 40,
        # 1.3e31 at 64, NaN at 128 -- i.e. ~3x per step), so full BPTT through the
        # sampled flip chain is numerically infeasible at the 200-step horizon that
        # t4 I5 asks for.  Forward value is unchanged either way (the added term is
        # exactly zero, ``relaxed - relaxed.detach()``).
        relaxed = (1 - prob) * x.detach() + prob * (1 - x.detach())
        x = flip + (relaxed - relaxed.detach())
        logits_last = logits
        if (step + 1) % decode_every == 0:
            last = (step + 1) == steps
            # The decode is a *reporting* operator: it runs to a fixed point, so
            # back-propagating through it multiplies by the adjacency matrix once per
            # iteration (mean degree ~80 on RB-suite graphs -> ~1e4-1e9 per graph).
            # Measured on GPU1 (fp32, K=20) with the decode on the graph: max |param
            # grad| 7.3e3 at 10 steps, 3.7e15 at 40, 3.7e24 at 64, NaN at 128 even
            # after the state path was detached, so the decode chain -- not the
            # rollout -- is what overflows.  It is therefore detached, and the
            # gradient comes from the single-step relaxed carrier below.
            size, decoded = decode_size(problem, x.detach(), adjacency, bias)
            sizes.append(float(size.mean().detach()))
            decode_steps.append(step + 1)
            if last:
                last_size = size
            if archive:
                if best_mask is None:
                    best_mask, best_size = decoded, size
                else:
                    better = size > best_size
                    best_mask = torch.where(better.unsqueeze(0), decoded, best_mask)
                    best_size = torch.where(better, size, best_size)
    return dict(state=x, logits=logits_last, sizes=sizes, decode_steps=decode_steps,
                last_size=last_size, archive_mask=best_mask, archive_size=best_size, steps=steps)


def unroll_objective(solver, graph, adjacency, topology, x0, *, steps, decode_every=DECODE_EVERY,
                     generator=None, logits_bias=None, archive=False):
    """``-mean(size)`` of the last decode; ``archive=True`` credits the best decode too.

    Scale: the frozen ``erdoes`` loss is ``-|S| + O(1)`` on a feasible set
    (``adjacency`` has no self loops, so ``A x = 0`` on an independent set), i.e.
    O(num_nodes).  ``loss = -mean(size)`` is therefore left un-normalised so the
    ``2e-5`` learning rate transfers from the erdoes recipe unchanged.
    """
    out = unroll(solver, graph, adjacency, topology, x0, steps=steps,
                 decode_every=decode_every, generator=generator, logits_bias=logits_bias,
                 archive=archive)
    if archive and out['archive_size'] is not None:
        value = out['archive_size'].mean()
    elif out['last_size'] is not None:
        value = out['last_size'].mean()
    else:
        size, _ = decode_size(solver.problem, out['state'].detach(), adjacency, graph.b)
        value = size.mean()
    out['value'] = value
    # Bounded surrogate: ``d loss / d theta`` is the one-step relaxed size gradient
    # ``-sum_nodes x`` (x carries only the ``relaxed - relaxed.detach()`` carrier, so
    # d x / d theta = (1-2x) d prob / d theta).  Forward value stays ``-mean(size)``
    # bit for bit because the carrier is exactly zero.
    surrogate = -out['state'].sum(dim=0).mean() if out['state'].requires_grad else 0.0
    out['loss'] = -value + (surrogate - surrogate.detach() if torch.is_tensor(surrogate)
                            else surrogate)
    return out


def _rollout_seed(solver, graph, counter):
    base = int(getattr(solver, 'seed', 0) or 0)
    idx = int(getattr(graph, 'idx', 0) or 0)
    return (base * 1_000_003 + idx * 7_919 + counter * 104_729) % (2 ** 63 - 1)


def generator_for(device, seed):
    gen = torch.Generator(device=device)
    gen.manual_seed(int(seed))
    return gen


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
# training hook: called from the additive branch in solvers.RLNN.train()
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
def configure(solver, args):
    """Attach the v11 unroll config to a solver (called once from ``models/main.py``).

    ``MetaSolver`` does not keep its namespace, so the additive ``loss == 'unroll'``
    block in ``main.py`` hands the argparse result over here before ``train()``.
    """
    solver.v11_unroll = _cfg(solver, args)
    return solver.v11_unroll


def _cfg(solver, args=None):
    cfg = getattr(solver, 'v11_unroll', None)
    if cfg is None:
        if args is None:
            args = getattr(solver, 'args', None)
        steps = int(getattr(args, 'unroll_steps', DEFAULT_STEPS) or DEFAULT_STEPS)
        cfg = dict(steps=steps, requested_steps=steps,
                   decode_every=int(getattr(args, 'unroll_decode_every', DECODE_EVERY)
                                    or DECODE_EVERY),
                   archive=bool(getattr(args, 'unroll_archive', False)),
                   degraded_reason=None, per_graph_s=None, peak_mem_bytes=None,
                   updates=0, measured=[], size_trace=[], loss_trace=[])
        solver.v11_unroll = cfg
    return cfg


def unroll_graph_loss(solver, graph, adjacency, topology, x):
    """One v11 C3 update on the particle columns ``x`` (shape ``num_nodes x K``).

    Drop-in replacement for the ``erdoes``/``reinforce`` loss terms; the caller
    (``solvers.RLNN.train``) keeps the surrounding optimizer step unchanged.
    The adaptive gates are measured on the first update only and can only *shrink*
    the unroll length for subsequent updates (recorded in ``run.json``).
    """
    cfg = _cfg(solver)
    device = x.device
    counter = cfg['updates']
    gen = generator_for(device, _rollout_seed(solver, graph, counter))
    first = not cfg['measured']

    if device.type == 'cuda':
        torch.cuda.synchronize(device)
        base_mem = torch.cuda.memory_allocated(device)
        torch.cuda.reset_peak_memory_stats(device)
    started = perf_counter()
    out = unroll_objective(solver, graph, adjacency, topology, x, steps=cfg['steps'],
                           decode_every=cfg['decode_every'], generator=gen,
                           archive=cfg['archive'])
    loss = out['loss']
    if device.type == 'cuda':
        torch.cuda.synchronize(device)
    elapsed = perf_counter() - started
    peak = (torch.cuda.max_memory_allocated(device) - base_mem) if device.type == 'cuda' else 0

    if first:
        cfg['per_graph_s'] = round(elapsed, 4)
        cfg['peak_mem_bytes'] = int(peak)
        cfg['measured'].append(dict(steps=cfg['steps'], per_graph_s=round(elapsed, 4),
                                    peak_mem_bytes=int(peak)))
        reasons = []
        if peak > MEMORY_GATE_BYTES:
            reasons.append(f'peak_mem {peak / 1024 ** 3:.2f}GB>6GB')
        if elapsed > TIME_GATE_SECONDS:
            reasons.append(f'per_graph {elapsed:.3f}s>0.6s')
        if reasons and cfg['steps'] > FALLBACK_STEPS:
            cfg['degraded_reason'] = '; '.join(reasons)
            cfg['steps'] = FALLBACK_STEPS
            cfg['measured'].append(dict(steps=FALLBACK_STEPS, degraded=True))

    cfg['updates'] = counter + 1
    cfg['size_trace'].append(round(float(out['sizes'][-1]), 4))
    cfg['loss_trace'].append(round(float(loss.item()), 4))
    return loss


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
# run.json snapshot
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
def _jsonable(value):
    if isinstance(value, Path):
        return str(value)
    if isinstance(value, (list, tuple)):
        return [_jsonable(item) for item in value]
    if isinstance(value, dict):
        return {str(key): _jsonable(item) for key, item in value.items()}
    if isinstance(value, (int, float, str, bool)) or value is None:
        return value
    return str(value)


def dump_run_json(args, solver, save_dir, extra=None):
    """Write ``run.json`` next to ``best.pt``: hyper-parameters + gate decisions."""
    cfg = getattr(solver, 'v11_unroll', {}) or {}
    payload = {
        'generated_at': datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat(),
        'argv': _jsonable({key: getattr(args, key) for key in sorted(vars(args))}),
        'loss': getattr(args, 'loss', None),
        'unroll': _jsonable({key: value for key, value in cfg.items()
                             if key not in ('size_trace', 'loss_trace')}),
        'unroll_size_trace': cfg.get('size_trace', [])[-20:],
        'unroll_loss_trace': cfg.get('loss_trace', [])[-20:],
        'torch': torch.__version__,
        'cuda': torch.version.cuda,
        'device_name': torch.cuda.get_device_name(0) if torch.cuda.is_available() else 'cpu',
        'peak_mem_bytes_total': int(torch.cuda.max_memory_allocated()) if torch.cuda.is_available() else 0,
    }
    accelerator = getattr(solver, 'accelerator', None)
    if accelerator is not None:
        payload['device'] = str(accelerator.device)
    if extra:
        payload.update(_jsonable(extra))
    path = Path(save_dir) / 'run.json'
    path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    path.write_text(json.dumps(payload, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False) + '\n', encoding='utf-8')
    return path


def config_snapshot(solver):
    """Compact one-line summary for logs."""
    cfg = getattr(solver, 'v11_unroll', {}) or {}
    peak = cfg.get('peak_mem_bytes')
    return (f"unroll steps={cfg.get('steps')} decode_every={cfg.get('decode_every')} "
            f"archive={cfg.get('archive')} per_graph={cfg.get('per_graph_s')}s "
            f"peak={(f'{peak / 1024 ** 3:.2f}GB' if peak else None)} "
            f"degraded={cfg.get('degraded_reason')}")


========================================================================
FILE: models/mis_v12_parallel.py
========================================================================
"""R2-E2: the parallel-arm batch multiplier ``c(N)`` and the N-arm ensemble arm.

R2 (variance route) lives or dies on one quantity: when ``N`` arms of the *same*
graph share one batched forward, how much does a step cost relative to a single
arm?  E1 (t14) fixed the variance side -- three full-budget seeds give a max-of-3
of ``+0.093`` -- and the budget side: splitting 808 steps into ``808/N`` costs
``-0.031`` (N=2) / ``-0.056`` (N=3).  So the arm breaks even only when

    N=2: c <= 1.60   (loose 1.79)      N=3: c <= 1.99   (loose 2.36)

Two modes, both on the frozen padded engine (``models/mis_v8_pad.py`` is on the
frozen list; nothing here edits it -- the engine is used as-is and the arms are
extra particle columns):

``bench``   E2-A: same graph, ``state`` widened to ``num_k = N*K`` columns, N in
            1..4, 200 steps each, median ms/step + a per-component breakdown
            (forward / energy / sampling / decode / rest) + peak memory.
``compare`` E2-B: 200 graphs, one session, single arm (810 steps, A0 flags) vs the
            parallel arm (N arms, ``floor(810/c)`` steps each, per-graph max),
            with per-graph CSV, paired bootstrap CI and a feasibility assertion
            on every returned set.

Arm independence: arms occupy consecutive column blocks and are initialised from
different torch seeds (1017/1019/1021, the project's eval seeds).  The noise
stream inside the captured block is a single ``torch.rand`` over all columns, so
an arm is *not* bit-identical to a standalone run of its seed -- column-level
noise is independent, the stream identity is not.  The parallel arm is therefore
the deployable statistic (N arms in one batch), not a re-derivation of E1's
max-over-three-standalone-runs; ``compare`` prints the per-arm sizes so the gap
between the two statistics is visible.

    python models/mis_v12_parallel.py bench   --arms 1 2 3 4 --steps 200
    python models/mis_v12_parallel.py compare --graphs 200 --c2 1.3 --c3 1.5
    python models/mis_v12_parallel.py compare --from_csv .../compare.csv --c2 2.389
"""
import argparse
import csv
import json
import math
import random
from pathlib import Path
from statistics import median
from time import perf_counter

import numpy as np
import torch

from diagnose_v7_census import build_parser as build_base_parser, solution_masks
from eval_v2 import dataset_at, load_policy, sync
from eval_v7_budget import run_pave
from eval_v8_capture_budget import paired_bootstrap
from eval_v8_padded import build_parser, decode_top_best, shape_of
from mis_v1 import adjacency
from mis_v3_search import SearchGraph
from mis_v3_value import PAVEV3
from mis_v7_recombine import is_independent
from mis_v8_pad import PaddedSearch
from v7_runs import pave

BASE_K = 200
BASE_STEPS = 810
ARM_SEEDS = (1017, 1019, 1021, 1023)


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
# shared plumbing
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
def parsed(argv):
    parser = build_parser()
    parser.add_argument("--bench_arms", type=int, nargs="+", default=[1, 2, 3, 4],
                        help="bench: arm counts to time")
    parser.add_argument("--bench_steps", type=int, default=200,
                        help="bench: steps per arm count")
    parser.add_argument("--graphs", type=int, default=200,
                        help="compare: graphs, taken in dataset order (no cherry-picking)")
    parser.add_argument("--c2", type=float, default=None, help="compare: measured c(2)")
    parser.add_argument("--c3", type=float, default=None, help="compare: measured c(3)")
    parser.add_argument("--decode_count", type=int, default=4,
                        help="A.3 decode this many lowest-energy particles (A0 uses 4)")
    parser.add_argument("--from_csv", default=None,
                        help="compare: recompute summary from an existing compare.csv")
    parser.add_argument("--out", default="outputs/v11/r2/e2_parallel",
                        help="output directory for the CSV/JSON artifacts")
    parser.set_defaults(budgets=[1.0], seeds=[1017], repeats=1, shards=1, shard=0,
                        decoders=["captured"])
    return parser.parse_args(argv)


def setup(args):
    """Solver + ranker + dataset, exactly the hooks ``eval_v8_padded`` uses."""
    solver = load_policy(args)
    solver.model.requires_grad_(False)
    checkpoint = torch.load(pave(args.reference_seed), map_location="cpu", weights_only=False)
    ranker = PAVEV3(checkpoint["mode"], checkpoint.get("stats_dim", 24))
    ranker.load_state_dict(checkpoint["model_state"])
    ranker = ranker.cpu().eval()
    dataset = dataset_at(args.test_path, solver.dtype, args.test_samples,
                         official=args.split == "test")
    solver.num_t = 20000
    return solver, ranker, dataset


def engine_for(solver, n_arms, n_max, capacity, args, device):
    """A padded engine whose particle columns hold ``n_arms`` blocks of K."""
    solver.num_k = BASE_K * n_arms
    engine = PaddedSearch(solver, n_max=n_max, capacity=capacity, chunk=args.chunk,
                          device=device, decode_chunk=args.decode_chunk, dense=args.dense)
    return engine


def arms_from(engine, n_arms, seed_of=None):
    """Re-initialise each K-column block from its own torch seed (after load())."""
    k = engine.num_k // n_arms
    for block in range(n_arms):
        seed = (seed_of or (lambda i: ARM_SEEDS[i]))(block)
        generator = torch.Generator(device=engine.device).manual_seed(int(seed))
        columns = slice(block * k, (block + 1) * k)
        engine.state[:, columns].copy_(
            torch.randint(0, 2, (engine.n_max, k), device=engine.device,
                          dtype=engine.dtype, generator=generator))
    engine.best_states.copy_(engine.state)
    engine.best_energy.copy_(engine.problem.energy_func(engine.adjacency, engine.bias,
                                                        engine.state)[0])
    engine.improvements.zero_()


def decode_arms(engine, adj, bias, n, n_arms, *, count=4):
    """Best mask per arm block: A.3 on the ``count`` lowest-energy particles."""
    k = engine.num_k // n_arms
    sizes, masks = [], []
    for block in range(n_arms):
        start = block * k
        energy = engine.best_energy[start:start + k].reshape(-1)
        index = torch.argsort(energy, dim=0)[: int(count)] + start
        subset = engine.best_states[:n][:, index].contiguous()
        solutions = engine.problem.decode_gradient_flip(subset, adj, bias,
                                                       return_solutions=True)
        column_sizes = solutions.sum(dim=0)
        best = int(torch.argmax(column_sizes))
        picked = solutions[:, best].to(torch.uint8).cpu().numpy()
        masks.append(int.from_bytes(np.packbits(picked, bitorder="little").tobytes(), "little"))
        sizes.append(int(column_sizes[best]))
    return sizes, masks


def pack_mask(problem, state, adj, bias, n):
    """Single-mask decode of ``state`` (used for the pre-run archive box)."""
    solutions = problem.decode_gradient_flip(state[:n], adj, bias, return_solutions=True)
    sizes = solutions.sum(dim=0)
    best = int(torch.argmax(sizes))
    picked = solutions[:, best].to(torch.uint8).cpu().numpy()
    return int.from_bytes(np.packbits(picked, bitorder="little").tobytes(), "little")


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
# mode 1: c(N)
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
def timed_blocks(engine, blocks, chunk):
    """Median ms/step of the captured block, one ``sync`` per block (A0 semantics)."""
    engine.graph_exec.replay()
    sync(engine.device)
    times = []
    for _ in range(blocks):
        started = perf_counter()
        engine.graph_exec.replay()
        torch.cuda.synchronize(engine.device)
        times.append((perf_counter() - started) * 1000.0 / chunk)
    return times


def timed_loop(function, iters, device):
    """Median-free amortised ms per call: ``iters`` calls, one sync at the end.

    Syncing inside the loop measures *latency* (a sync costs ~0.4 ms on this
    card), which is not what a captured block pays: inside one replay the ten
    steps are enqueued back to back.  Amortising over a loop is the comparable
    number.
    """
    function()
    sync(device)
    started = perf_counter()
    for _ in range(int(iters)):
        function()
    sync(device)
    return (perf_counter() - started) * 1000.0 / int(iters)


def breakdown(engine, iters, device, adj, bias, n):
    """Per-component cost of one *step*, amortised (no per-call sync)."""
    state = engine.state
    k = engine.num_k
    dense_raw = torch.zeros((engine.n_max, engine.n_max), dtype=engine.dtype, device=device)
    dense_raw.index_put_((engine.slots, engine.col), engine.raw)

    def forward():
        engine._logits()

    def energy_csr():
        engine.problem.energy_func(engine.adjacency, engine.bias, state)

    def energy_dense():
        engine.problem.energy_func(dense_raw, engine.bias, state)

    def sample():
        probs = torch.div(engine._logits(), engine.temperature).sigmoid()
        noise = torch.rand(state.shape, device=device, dtype=engine.dtype,
                           generator=engine.generator)
        flipped = torch.where(noise < probs, 1 - state, state) * engine.keep
        state.copy_(flipped)

    def decode():
        decode_arms(engine, adj, bias, n, 1, count=4)

    return dict(forward=timed_loop(forward, iters, device),
                energy_csr=timed_loop(energy_csr, iters, device),
                energy_dense=timed_loop(energy_dense, iters, device),
                sample=timed_loop(sample, iters, device),
                decode=timed_loop(decode, max(5, iters // 10), device))


def bench(args):
    solver, _ranker, dataset = setup(args)
    device = solver.accelerator.device
    n_max, capacity = shape_of(dataset, args.padded_shapes)
    graph = dataset[0].to(device)
    edges = graph.edge_index
    n = int(graph.num_nodes)
    adj, bias = adjacency(graph), graph.b
    print(f"bench: graph_000000 nodes={n} edges={edges.shape[1]} "
          f"n_max={n_max} capacity={capacity} num_k_base={BASE_K}", flush=True)
    blocks = max(1, int(args.bench_steps) // int(args.chunk))
    rows = []
    for n_arms in args.bench_arms:
        torch.cuda.empty_cache()
        torch.cuda.reset_peak_memory_stats()
        engine = engine_for(solver, n_arms, n_max, capacity, args, device)
        engine.load(graph, edges, ARM_SEEDS[0])
        arms_from(engine, n_arms)
        times = timed_blocks(engine, blocks, args.chunk)
        step_ms = median(times)
        parts = breakdown(engine, 50, device, adj, bias, n)
        peak = torch.cuda.max_memory_allocated(device) / 2 ** 30
        step_parts = parts["forward"] + parts["energy_csr"] + parts["sample"]
        row = dict(n_arms=n_arms, num_k=engine.num_k, steps=blocks * int(args.chunk),
                   ms_step=round(step_ms, 4), ms_block=round(step_ms * int(args.chunk), 4),
                   p10=round(float(np.percentile(times, 10)), 4),
                   p90=round(float(np.percentile(times, 90)), 4),
                   peak_gib=round(peak, 3),
                   forward=round(parts["forward"], 4),
                   energy_csr=round(parts["energy_csr"], 4),
                   energy_dense=round(parts["energy_dense"], 4),
                   sample=round(parts["sample"], 4),
                   decode=round(parts["decode"], 4),
                   eager_sum=round(step_parts, 4),
                   captured_minus_eager=round(step_ms - step_parts, 4))
        rows.append(row)
        print(json.dumps(row), flush=True)
        del engine
    base = rows[0]["ms_step"]
    for row in rows:
        row["c"] = round(row["ms_step"] / base, 4)
    out = Path(args.out)
    out.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    payload = dict(protocol=dict(num_k_base=BASE_K, steps_bench=blocks * int(args.chunk),
                                 chunk=args.chunk, dense=bool(args.dense),
                                 dtype=str(solver.dtype), graph=f"graph_000000",
                                 nodes=n, n_max=n_max, capacity=capacity,
                                 seeds=list(ARM_SEEDS[:max(args.bench_arms)])),
                   rows=rows,
                   verdict=dict(n2_c=next(r["c"] for r in rows if r["n_arms"] == 2)
                                if any(r["n_arms"] == 2 for r in rows) else None,
                                n3_c=next(r["c"] for r in rows if r["n_arms"] == 3)
                                if any(r["n_arms"] == 3 for r in rows) else None,
                                n2_threshold=1.60, n3_threshold=1.99))
    (out / "c_N.json").write_text(json.dumps(payload, indent=1), encoding="utf-8")
    print(f"wrote {out / 'c_N.json'}", flush=True)
    return 0


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
# mode 2: 200-graph single vs parallel
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
def _numeric(value):
    """CSV cells come back as strings; recover numbers for the summary maths."""
    text = str(value).strip()
    if not text:
        return value
    try:
        return int(text) if text.lstrip("-").isdigit() else float(text)
    except ValueError:
        return value


def compare(args):
    if getattr(args, "from_csv", None):
        with Path(args.from_csv).open(newline="", encoding="utf-8") as handle:
            rows = [{key: _numeric(value) for key, value in row.items()}
                    for row in csv.DictReader(handle)]
        plans = [(1, BASE_STEPS)]
        for n_arms, c in ((2, args.c2), (3, args.c3)):
            if c is None:
                continue
            plans.append((n_arms, int(math.floor(BASE_STEPS / float(c)) // args.chunk
                                      * args.chunk)))
        print(f"compare: reused {len(rows)} rows from {args.from_csv}, "
              f"plans={[(n, s) for n, s in plans]}", flush=True)
        return analyse(args, rows, plans)
    solver, ranker, dataset = setup(args)
    device = solver.accelerator.device
    n_max, capacity = shape_of(dataset, args.padded_shapes)
    graphs = min(int(args.graphs), len(dataset))
    c2 = float(args.c2 if args.c2 is not None else 1.0)
    c3 = float(args.c3 if args.c3 is not None else 1.0)
    plans = [(1, BASE_STEPS)]
    for n_arms, c in ((2, c2), (3, c3)):
        if args.c2 is None and n_arms == 2 or args.c3 is None and n_arms == 3:
            continue
        plans.append((n_arms, int(math.floor(BASE_STEPS / c) // args.chunk * args.chunk)))
    engines = {n_arms: engine_for(solver, n_arms, n_max, capacity, args, device)
               for n_arms, _ in plans}
    print(f"compare: {graphs} graphs, plans={[(n, s) for n, s in plans]}, "
          f"n_max={n_max} capacity={capacity}", flush=True)
    rows = []
    for position in range(graphs):
        graph = dataset[position].to(device)
        edges = graph.edge_index
        n = int(graph.num_nodes)
        adj, bias = adjacency(graph), graph.b
        topology = SearchGraph(n, edges, seed=1017)
        record = dict(graph_id=Path(dataset.files[position]).stem, nodes=n, edges=int(edges.shape[1]))
        for n_arms, steps in plans:
            engine = engines[n_arms]
            tick = perf_counter()
            engine.load(graph, edges, ARM_SEEDS[0])
            arms_from(engine, n_arms)
            blocks = max(1, steps // int(args.chunk))
            started = perf_counter()
            engine.run(float("inf"), lambda states: None, max_blocks=blocks,
                       decode_every=blocks + 1, sync_each_block=True)
            sync(device)
            search_seconds = perf_counter() - started
            sizes, masks = decode_arms(engine, adj, bias, n, n_arms, count=args.decode_count)
            tag = "single" if n_arms == 1 else f"par{n_arms}"
            record[f"{tag}_search"] = max(sizes)
            record[f"{tag}_arms"] = "/".join(str(size) for size in sizes)
            record[f"{tag}_steps"] = blocks * int(args.chunk)
            record[f"{tag}_ms"] = round(search_seconds * 1000.0 / (blocks * int(args.chunk)), 4)
            best_mask = masks[int(np.argmax(sizes))]
            if not is_independent(best_mask, topology.neighbors):
                raise ValueError(f"{record['graph_id']}: illegal set in {tag}")
            deadline = perf_counter() + min(args.post_reserve, 0.2 * 1.0)
            final = run_pave(topology, best_mask, ranker, args, deadline)
            sync(device)
            if not is_independent(final, topology.neighbors):
                raise ValueError(f"{record['graph_id']}: illegal PAVE set in {tag}")
            record[f"{tag}_final"] = final.bit_count()
            record[f"{tag}_wall"] = round(perf_counter() - tick, 4)
        rows.append(record)
        if position % 20 == 0 or position + 1 == graphs:
            print(f"  [{position + 1}/{graphs}] {record['graph_id']} "
                  f"single={record['single_search']}/{record['single_final']} "
                  + " ".join(f"{tag}={record[f'{tag}_search']}/{record[f'{tag}_final']}"
                             for tag, _ in ((f"par{n}", s) for n, s in plans)
                             if f"{tag}_search" in record),
                  flush=True)
    return analyse(args, rows, plans)


def analyse(args, rows, plans):
    out = Path(args.out)
    out.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    fields = list(rows[0])
    with (out / "compare.csv").open("w", newline="", encoding="utf-8") as handle:
        writer = csv.DictWriter(handle, fieldnames=fields)
        writer.writeheader()
        writer.writerows(rows)
    summary = dict(graphs=len(rows), plans=[[n, s] for n, s in plans], delta={})
    for n_arms, steps in plans:
        if n_arms == 1:
            continue
        tag = f"par{n_arms}"
        for column in ("search", "final"):
            pairs = [(row[f"{tag}_{column}"], row[f"single_{column}"]) for row in rows]
            delta = [a - b for a, b in pairs]
            boot_mean, low, high = paired_bootstrap(delta, 5000, 1017)
            summary["delta"][f"{tag}_{column}"] = dict(
                mean=round(float(np.mean(delta)), 4), boot_mean=round(float(boot_mean), 4),
                ci=[round(low, 4), round(high, 4)],
                steps_per_arm=steps, wins=sum(1 for value in delta if value > 0),
                losses=sum(1 for value in delta if value < 0),
                ties=sum(1 for value in delta if value == 0))
    summary["mean_ms"] = {key: round(float(np.mean([row[key] for row in rows])), 4)
                          for key in fields if key.endswith("_ms")}
    (out / "summary.json").write_text(json.dumps(summary, indent=1), encoding="utf-8")
    print(json.dumps(summary, indent=1), flush=True)
    return 0


def main(argv=None):
    import sys
    argv = list(sys.argv[1:] if argv is None else argv)
    mode = argv[0] if argv else "bench"
    args = parsed(argv[1:])
    return bench(args) if mode == "bench" else compare(args)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main())


========================================================================
FILE: models/mis_v13_profile.py
========================================================================
"""R2-E3 (t17): kernel-level profile of the A0 one-step path.

Measurement only.  Nothing here touches the model, the weights, ``K``,
``decode_every`` or any numerical path: the script builds the *same* engine the
A0 gate uses (``--dense --mixed_precision fp16 --num_k 200 --chunk 10``),
replays the captured block, and reads the CUDA kernel table out of
``torch.profiler``.  It never writes into a run directory, only into
``--out``.

What it answers, for the "is there 2x of step throughput left" call:

(A) where the ~0.87 ms/step goes: top kernels (share of device time,
    calls per step, us per call) for the captured block and for the eager
    path -- the eager path issues the same arithmetic without the graph, so the
    difference between the two is the launch/scheduling share;
    plus the achieved GFLOP/s of the 264x264x200 GEMM against the card's fp16
    tensor peak, and a same-shape ``torch.matmul`` micro-benchmark, which is
    the cheapest available estimate of what a better kernel could reach at
    this size.

(B) the ceiling of the three speed-up families, each backed by a measured
    number: fewer launches (captured vs eager gap), different math (same-shape
    gemm at fp16/bf16/fp32 -- the dtype ladder the kernels actually deliver),
    reuse across graphs (capture cost amortised over the 1000 graphs).

(C) whether >=2x step throughput is reachable without changing the model.

    CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=1 python models/mis_v13_profile.py \
        --out outputs/v11/r2/e3_profile
"""
import argparse
import json
from pathlib import Path
from statistics import median
from time import perf_counter

import torch
from torch.profiler import ProfilerActivity, profile
from torch.utils.flop_counter import FlopCounterMode

from eval_v2 import dataset_at, load_policy, sync
from eval_v8_padded import build_parser, shape_of
from mis_v12_parallel import engine_for

# Board spec sheets, dense (no sparsity) fp16/bf16 tensor throughput, TFLOPS.
# Only used for the utilisation ratio; the ratio is a sanity check, not a claim.
PEAK_FP16_TFLOPS = {
    "NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5090": 209.5,
    "NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4090": 165.2,
    "NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3090": 71.0,
    "NVIDIA A100-SXM4-40GB": 312.0,
    "NVIDIA H100 PCIe": 756.0,
}


def parse(argv):
    parser = build_parser()
    parser.add_argument("--graph_index", type=int, default=0,
                        help="dataset index to profile (dataset order, no cherry-picking)")
    parser.add_argument("--blocks", type=int, default=20,
                        help="captured blocks to profile (one block = --chunk steps; 20 = 200 steps)")
    parser.add_argument("--eager_steps", type=int, default=50,
                        help="eager steps to profile")
    parser.add_argument("--warm_blocks", type=int, default=5,
                        help="warm-up blocks before the captured profile")
    parser.add_argument("--top", type=int, default=15, help="kernels to keep per table")
    parser.add_argument("--out", default="outputs/v11/r2/e3_profile",
                        help="directory for kernels.json")
    # The A0 gate configuration, pinned here so the profile cannot silently
    # measure a different path: fp16 + dense + K=200 + chunk 10 (the shell
    # script's ``COMMON`` flags, see ``train_scripts/v11/a0_gate0.sh``).
    parser.set_defaults(budgets=[1.0], seeds=[1017], repeats=1, shards=1, shard=0,
                        decoders=["captured"], num_k=200, chunk=10, dense=True,
                        mixed_precision="fp16", reference_seed=0,
                        save_dir=Path("outputs/v2/none_seed0/checkpoints"),
                        result_dir=Path("tmp/e3_profile_unused"))
    # ``--result_dir`` / ``--reference_seed`` are argparse-required in the eval
    # parser; this script writes no run directory, so their defaults suffice.
    for action in parser._actions:
        if action.dest in {"result_dir", "reference_seed"}:
            action.required = False
    return parser.parse_args(argv)


def device_report(device):
    properties = torch.cuda.get_device_properties(device)
    name = properties.name
    peak = PEAK_FP16_TFLOPS.get(name)
    return dict(name=name, sm_count=int(properties.multi_processor_count),
                total_gib=round(properties.total_memory / 1024 ** 3, 3),
                capability=f"{properties.major}.{properties.minor}",
                peak_fp16_tflops=peak,
                torch=torch.__version__, cuda=torch.version.cuda)


def analytic_gemm_flops(model, nodes, k):
    """FLOPs of the graph matmuls only (``adj @ support``), from module shapes.

    Every ``GCNConv`` in this family multiplies ``(nodes, nodes)`` by
    ``(nodes*k, hidden)``, i.e. ``2*nodes*nodes*k*hidden`` FLOPs per step.
    """
    total, layers = 0, []
    for module in model.modules():
        if module.__class__.__name__ != "GCNConv":
            continue
        hidden = module.out_features
        flops = 2 * nodes * nodes * k * hidden
        total += flops
        layers.append(dict(in_features=module.in_features, out_features=hidden,
                           flops=flops))
    return total, layers


def model_report(model):
    linear = [(m.in_features, m.out_features) for m in model.modules()
              if isinstance(m, torch.nn.Linear)]
    return dict(parameters=int(sum(p.numel() for p in model.parameters())),
                linears=len(linear), linear_shapes=linear[:6],
                convs=sum(1 for m in model.modules()
                          if m.__class__.__name__ == "GCNConv"))


def group_of(name):
    """Which part of the step a kernel belongs to (name heuristics)."""
    lowered = name.lower()
    if any(tag in lowered for tag in ("gemm", "cutlass", "csrmm", "spmm", "gemv", "gemmk1")):
        return "gemm"
    if any(tag in lowered for tag in ("reduce", "softmax")):
        return "reduce"
    if any(tag in lowered for tag in ("rand", "philox", "distribution")):
        return "sample"
    if any(tag in lowered for tag in ("elementwise", "memcpy", "copy", "fill", "cast")):
        return "pointwise"
    return "other"


def group_rows(rows):
    groups = {}
    for row in rows:
        key = group_of(row["name"])
        bucket = groups.setdefault(key, dict(us_per_step=0.0, kernels=0, calls_per_step=0.0))
        bucket["us_per_step"] += row["device_us_per_step"]
        bucket["kernels"] += 1
        bucket["calls_per_step"] += row["count_per_step"]
    for bucket in groups.values():
        bucket["us_per_step"] = round(bucket["us_per_step"], 2)
        bucket["calls_per_step"] = round(bucket["calls_per_step"], 2)
    return groups


def kernel_rows(profiler, steps, top):
    """Top device-time kernels, normalised per step."""
    rows = []
    for event in profiler.key_averages():
        device_us = float(getattr(event, "self_device_time_total", 0.0))
        if device_us <= 0.0:
            continue
        cpu_us = float(getattr(event, "self_cpu_time_total", 0.0))
        calls = int(event.count)
        rows.append(dict(name=event.key, device_us_per_step=device_us / steps,
                         device_us_per_call=device_us / calls,
                         count_per_step=calls / steps,
                         cpu_us_per_step=cpu_us / steps))
    total = sum(row["device_us_per_step"] for row in rows)
    for row in rows:
        row["share"] = row["device_us_per_step"] / total if total else 0.0
    rows.sort(key=lambda row: row["device_us_per_step"], reverse=True)
    return rows[:top], rows, total


def timed_blocks(engine, blocks, chunk):
    """Wall ms/step of the captured block (A0 semantics: one sync per block)."""
    engine.graph_exec.replay()
    sync(engine.device)
    times = []
    for _ in range(blocks):
        started = perf_counter()
        engine.graph_exec.replay()
        torch.cuda.synchronize(engine.device)
        times.append((perf_counter() - started) * 1000.0 / chunk)
    return times


def micro_gemm(nodes, k, hidden, device, dtypes, iters=50):
    """Same-shape ``adj @ support`` through cuBLAS: the kernel ceiling at this size."""
    adj = torch.rand((nodes, nodes), device=device)
    # ``GCNConv`` flattens ``(nodes, k, hidden)`` to ``(nodes, k*hidden)`` before
    # the adjacency matmul, so the contract is (nodes, nodes) x (nodes, k*hidden).
    support = torch.rand((nodes, k * hidden), device=device)
    results = {}
    for dtype in dtypes:
        left = adj.to(dtype)
        right = support.to(dtype)
        for _ in range(5):
            torch.matmul(left, right)
        sync(device)
        started = perf_counter()
        for _ in range(iters):
            torch.matmul(left, right)
        sync(device)
        seconds = perf_counter() - started
        flops = 2 * nodes * nodes * k * hidden
        results[str(dtype).replace("torch.", "")] = dict(
            ms=seconds * 1000.0 / iters,
            gflops=flops * iters / seconds / 1e9)
    return results


def main():
    args = parse(None)
    out = Path(args.out)
    out.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    device = torch.device("cuda" if torch.cuda.is_available() else "cpu")
    if device.type != "cuda":
        raise SystemExit("this profile needs CUDA (a CPU run measures nothing)")

    solver = load_policy(args)
    solver.model.requires_grad_(False)
    dataset = dataset_at(args.test_path, solver.dtype, args.test_samples,
                         official=args.split == "test")
    n_max, capacity = shape_of(dataset, args.padded_shapes)
    graph = dataset[args.graph_index]
    nodes = int(graph.num_nodes)
    print(f"graph {args.graph_index}: nodes {nodes}, padded {n_max}/{capacity}", flush=True)

    # --- capture cost + engine (identical flags to the A0 gate) ------------
    entered = perf_counter()
    engine = engine_for(solver, 1, n_max, capacity, args, device)
    capture_seconds = perf_counter() - entered
    engine.load(graph.to(device), graph.edge_index, args.seeds[0])
    engine.run(perf_counter() + 0.05, lambda states: None)
    sync(device)
    solver.num_t = 20000
    chunk = engine.chunk
    steps_captured = args.blocks * chunk
    print(f"capture {capture_seconds:.3f} s, chunk {chunk}, "
          f"num_k {engine.num_k}, dtype {engine.dtype}, dense {engine.use_dense}", flush=True)

    # --- wall clock (outside the profiler) --------------------------------
    for _ in range(args.warm_blocks):
        engine.graph_exec.replay()
    sync(device)
    wall_captured = timed_blocks(engine, args.blocks, chunk)
    wall_per_step = median(wall_captured)

    # --- (A) captured kernel table ---------------------------------------
    # CUPTI registers itself on the first profiled region and that region comes
    # back empty, so burn one block on a throw-away profile first.
    with profile(activities=[ProfilerActivity.CPU, ProfilerActivity.CUDA]) as warm:
        engine.graph_exec.replay()
        torch.cuda.synchronize(device)
    warm_events = sum(1 for _ in warm.key_averages())
    with profile(activities=[ProfilerActivity.CPU, ProfilerActivity.CUDA]) as captured:
        for _ in range(args.blocks):
            engine.graph_exec.replay()
        torch.cuda.synchronize(device)
    rows_captured, all_captured, kernel_captured = kernel_rows(captured, steps_captured, args.top)
    print(f"profiler: warm-up region {warm_events} rows, captured region "
          f"{len(list(captured.key_averages()))} rows", flush=True)

    # --- (A) eager kernel table ------------------------------------------
    # ``_body_one`` is the same arithmetic with ``chunk = 1`` and no capture:
    # every step goes through the host launch path, which is exactly the
    # launch/scheduling share the graph removes.
    for _ in range(5):
        engine._body_one()
    sync(device)
    started = perf_counter()
    for _ in range(args.eager_steps):
        engine._body_one()
    sync(device)
    wall_eager = (perf_counter() - started) * 1000.0 / args.eager_steps
    with profile(activities=[ProfilerActivity.CPU, ProfilerActivity.CUDA]) as eager:
        for _ in range(args.eager_steps):
            engine._body_one()
        torch.cuda.synchronize(device)
    rows_eager, all_eager, kernel_eager = kernel_rows(eager, args.eager_steps, args.top)

    # --- FLOPs per step ---------------------------------------------------
    with FlopCounterMode(display=False) as counter:
        engine._body_one()
    flops_counter = int(counter.get_total_flops())
    gemm_flops, gemm_layers = analytic_gemm_flops(solver.model, n_max, engine.num_k)

    def gemm_share(rows):
        return sum(row["device_us_per_step"] for row in rows
                   if "gemm" in row["name"].lower() or "cutlass" in row["name"].lower()
                   or "matmul" in row["name"].lower())

    captured_gemm_us = gemm_share(all_captured)
    eager_gemm_us = gemm_share(all_eager)
    achieved = dict(
        flops_per_step=flops_counter,
        gemm_flops_per_step=gemm_flops,
        gemm_layers=len(gemm_layers),
        gemm_us_per_step_captured=captured_gemm_us,
        gemm_us_per_step_eager=eager_gemm_us,
        gflops_gemm_captured=(gemm_flops / (captured_gemm_us * 1e-6) / 1e9
                              if captured_gemm_us > 0 else None),
        gflops_gemm_eager=(gemm_flops / (eager_gemm_us * 1e-6) / 1e9
                           if eager_gemm_us > 0 else None),
        gflops_step_captured=flops_counter / (wall_per_step * 1e-3) / 1e9,
    )

    # --- (B) kernel ceiling at this shape --------------------------------
    hidden = gemm_layers[0]["out_features"] if gemm_layers else 100
    micro = micro_gemm(n_max, engine.num_k, hidden, device,
                       (torch.float16, torch.bfloat16, torch.float32))
    groups_captured = group_rows(all_captured)
    groups_eager = group_rows(all_eager)
    kernels_per_step = sum(row["count_per_step"] for row in all_captured)
    elementwise = [row["device_us_per_call"] for row in all_captured
                   if group_of(row["name"]) in ("pointwise", "sample", "reduce")]
    min_kernel_us = min(elementwise) if elementwise else None
    # A speed-up ceiling, spelled out: every gemm at the micro-benchmark rate,
    # every pointwise/reduce kernel at the *measured* minimum kernel latency
    # (i.e. perfect fusion into one launch each, zero DRAM cost).
    gemm_floor_us = gemm_flops / (micro["float16"]["gflops"] * 1e3)
    latency_floor_us = kernels_per_step * min_kernel_us if min_kernel_us else None
    other_us = sum(bucket["us_per_step"] for key, bucket in groups_captured.items()
                   if key not in ("gemm", "pointwise", "sample", "reduce"))
    floor = dict(kernels_per_step=round(kernels_per_step, 2),
                 min_elementwise_kernel_us=round(min_kernel_us, 3) if min_kernel_us else None,
                 gemm_floor_us=round(gemm_floor_us, 1),
                 latency_floor_us=round(latency_floor_us, 1) if latency_floor_us else None,
                 other_us=round(other_us, 1))
    if latency_floor_us:
        best_case_us = gemm_floor_us + latency_floor_us + other_us
        floor["best_case_ms_per_step"] = round(best_case_us / 1000.0, 4)
        floor["speedup_ceiling"] = round(wall_per_step / (best_case_us / 1000.0), 2)
    report = dict(
        graph_index=args.graph_index, nodes=nodes, padded=(n_max, capacity),
        num_k=int(engine.num_k), chunk=int(chunk), dtype=str(engine.dtype),
        dense=bool(engine.use_dense),
        capture_seconds=round(capture_seconds, 4),
        steps_captured=steps_captured, steps_eager=args.eager_steps,
        wall_ms_per_step_captured=wall_per_step,
        wall_ms_per_step_captured_all=wall_captured,
        wall_ms_per_step_eager=wall_eager,
        kernel_ms_per_step_captured=kernel_captured / 1000.0,
        kernel_ms_per_step_eager=kernel_eager / 1000.0,
        gap_ms_per_step_captured=wall_per_step - kernel_captured / 1000.0,
        launch_gap_share=(wall_per_step - kernel_captured / 1000.0) / wall_per_step,
        eager_over_captured=wall_eager / wall_per_step,
        kernels_captured=rows_captured, kernels_eager=rows_eager,
        groups_captured=groups_captured, groups_eager=groups_eager, floor=floor,
        achieved=achieved, micro_gemm=micro, micro_shape=(n_max, engine.num_k, hidden),
        model=model_report(solver.model), device=device_report(device),
        builder="models/mis_v13_profile.py",
    )
    peak_gflops = (device_report(device)["peak_fp16_tflops"] or 0.0) * 1000.0
    report["achieved"]["peak_fraction"] = (
        (achieved["gflops_gemm_captured"] or 0.0) / peak_gflops if peak_gflops else None)
    report["achieved"]["gflops_step_peak_fraction"] = (
        achieved["gflops_step_captured"] / peak_gflops if peak_gflops else None)
    report["floor"]["speedup_ceiling"] = floor.get("speedup_ceiling")
    path = out / "kernels.json"
    path.write_text(json.dumps(report, indent=1), encoding="utf-8")

    print(f"\nwall {wall_per_step:.4f} ms/step (captured), eager {wall_eager:.4f}")
    print(f"device busy {report['kernel_ms_per_step_captured']:.4f} ms/step "
          f"=> gap {report['gap_ms_per_step_captured']:.4f} "
          f"({report['launch_gap_share']:.1%})")
    print(f"flops/step {flops_counter/1e6:.2f} MFLOP, gemm {gemm_flops/1e6:.2f} MFLOP "
          f"in {captured_gemm_us:.1f} us => "
          f"{achieved['gflops_gemm_captured'] or float('nan'):.1f} GFLOP/s "
          f"({report['achieved']['peak_fraction'] or 0.0:.1%} of peak)")
    print("\ntop kernels (captured):")
    for row in rows_captured[:args.top]:
        print(f"  {row['share']:6.1%} {row['count_per_step']:6.2f}/step "
              f"{row['device_us_per_call']:8.1f} us/call  {row['name'][:70]}")
    print("\nper group (captured):", json.dumps(groups_captured))
    print("floor:", json.dumps(floor))
    print("\nmicro gemm (same shape):", json.dumps(micro))
    print(f"\nwrote {path}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

"""Bounded improving exchanges on a legal MIS solution."""
from itertools import combinations, islice
from math import fsum, inf, log1p
from time import perf_counter
from typing import NamedTuple


def nodes(mask):
    while mask:
        bit = mask & -mask
        yield bit.bit_length() - 1
        mask ^= bit


def node_mask(indices):
    return sum(1 << node for node in indices)


class Exchange(NamedTuple):
    removed: tuple
    added: tuple
    release_count: int


class ExchangeGraph:
    def __init__(self, num_nodes, edge_index):
        self.neighbors = [0] * num_nodes
        for source, target in zip(*edge_index.tolist()):
            self.neighbors[source] |= 1 << target
        self.all_nodes = (1 << num_nodes) - 1
        self.log_degree = [log1p(row.bit_count()) for row in self.neighbors]
        self.greedy_order = sorted(range(num_nodes), key=self.log_degree.__getitem__)

    def feasible(self, selected):
        return all(not self.neighbors[node] & selected for node in nodes(selected))

    def extend(self, selected):
        available = self.all_nodes ^ selected
        for node in nodes(selected):
            available &= ~self.neighbors[node]
        for node in self.greedy_order:
            bit = 1 << node
            if available & bit:
                selected |= bit
                available &= ~(bit | self.neighbors[node])
        return selected

    def _exchanges(self, selected, size, deadline):
        singles = {}
        doubles = {}
        for node in nodes(self.all_nodes ^ selected):
            blockers = self.neighbors[node] & selected
            count = blockers.bit_count()
            if count == 1:
                singles[blockers] = singles.get(blockers, 0) | (1 << node)
            elif size == 2 and count == 2:
                doubles[blockers] = doubles.get(blockers, 0) | (1 << node)

        for removed in combinations(nodes(selected), size):
            if perf_counter() >= deadline:
                return
            if size == 1:
                released = singles.get(1 << removed[0], 0)
            else:
                first, second = (1 << node for node in removed)
                released = singles.get(first, 0) | singles.get(second, 0) | doubles.get(first | second, 0)
            release_count = released.bit_count()
            while released:
                if perf_counter() >= deadline:
                    return
                first = released & -released
                released ^= first
                u = first.bit_length() - 1
                compatible = released & ~self.neighbors[u]
                if size == 1:
                    for v in nodes(compatible):
                        yield Exchange(removed, (u, v), release_count)
                else:
                    while compatible:
                        second = compatible & -compatible
                        compatible ^= second
                        v = second.bit_length() - 1
                        for w in nodes(compatible & ~self.neighbors[v]):
                            yield Exchange(removed, (u, v, w), release_count)

    def actions(self, selected, *, cap=None, larger=False, deadline=inf):
        actions = list(islice(self._exchanges(selected, 1, deadline), cap))
        if not actions and larger:
            actions = list(islice(self._exchanges(selected, 2, deadline), cap))
        return actions

    def apply(self, selected, action):
        candidate = (selected & ~node_mask(action.removed)) | node_mask(action.added)
        candidate = self.extend(candidate)
        if candidate.bit_count() <= selected.bit_count() or not self.feasible(candidate):
            raise ValueError("Exchange must produce a larger independent set")
        return candidate

    def coverage(self, selected, action):
        available = self.all_nodes & ~(selected | node_mask(action.added))
        neighborhoods = [self.neighbors[node] & available for node in action.added]
        union, shared = 0, 0
        for row in neighborhoods:
            shared |= union & row
            union |= row
        return union.bit_count(), shared.bit_count(), [row.bit_count() for row in neighborhoods]

    def heuristic(self, selected, action):
        covered, _, _ = self.coverage(selected, action)
        return covered, -action.release_count

    def features(self, selected, action):
        added_degree = [self.log_degree[node] for node in action.added]
        covered, shared, remaining = self.coverage(selected, action)
        remaining = [log1p(count) for count in remaining]
        return (fsum(self.log_degree[node] for node in action.removed), fsum(added_degree),
                max(added_degree) - min(added_degree), log1p(action.release_count),
                fsum(remaining), max(remaining) - min(remaining), log1p(covered),
                log1p(shared), len(action.removed))


def improve(graph, selected, *, cap, rounds, larger=False, deadline=inf, choose=None, repeat_choice=False):
    """Choose the first action, then use the shared degree/coverage rule."""
    changes = 0
    candidate_count = 0
    for step in range(rounds):
        if perf_counter() >= deadline:
            break
        actions = graph.actions(selected, cap=cap, larger=larger, deadline=deadline)
        if step == 0:
            candidate_count = len(actions)
        if not actions or perf_counter() >= deadline:
            break
        if choose is not None and (step == 0 or repeat_choice):
            action = choose(graph, selected, actions)
        else:
            action = min(actions, key=lambda a: graph.heuristic(selected, a))
        candidate = graph.apply(selected, action)
        if perf_counter() >= deadline:
            break
        selected = candidate
        changes += 1
    return selected, changes, candidate_count


def action_values(graph, selected, actions, *, cap, rounds, larger=False):
    values = []
    for action in actions:
        successor = graph.apply(selected, action)
        final, _, _ = improve(graph, successor, cap=cap, rounds=rounds - 1, larger=larger)
        values.append(final.bit_count())
    return values
